hero: Confidence in business is mostly just knowing your own numbers.
sub: The owner who prices a job on the spot is not braver than you. He knows what the last one cost him, because somebody wrote it down at the time.

hero: You find out what you owe early enough to put the money aside.
sub: We do your figures while there is still room to plan for them, so the amount reaches you in good time, in plain words, with the reference you need to pay it.

hero: A local office you can walk into.
sub: We are on Washwood Heath Road in Saltley, B8 1RB. Bring the folder, sit down with it, and sort it out with someone who is actually in Birmingham.

hero: A straight answer the same day, in words you can use.
sub: Message us and a person reads it, not a queue. You get a plain answer you can act on, in writing, so you can find it again when the same thing comes up in March.

hero: Selling second-hand, VAT-registered? VAT is one-sixth of the margin.
sub: You can choose it for second-hand goods, art, antiques or collectors' items bought with no VAT charged. Not metals, gold or stones, or anything you paid VAT on.

hero: The deductions you took in the last tax month are due by the 22nd.
sub: HMRC counts it paid when cleared funds arrive by the 22nd; a posted cheque by the 19th. A different cycle: under £1,500 a month on average, you may pay quarterly.

hero: Take on your first employee and you need £5 million of cover.
sub: Excluded: a one-director company where the director owns at least half the shares, an employer whose only employee is close family, and a sole trader with no employees.

setup: I asked a shopkeeper when he last put his prices up.
punch: He pointed at the sign. Still perfectly readable.
hook: A readable sign is not a price. Work out what the job costs you now, not in 2019, and then decide what it is worth.

setup: He rang at ten past eight on the morning of 30 January.
punch: Quick one. Did I ever register?
hook: Nothing gets found quickly on the day. Keep the year where someone else could pick it up, and there is no panic to have.

line: Beware of little expenses; a small leak will sink a great ship.
